messages:
mae: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to demarcate hotpath dependencies. Goal: shrink the real-time surface (hotpath-core) and move enrichment/personalization to an isolated lane to reduce tail latency and make tech-debt paydown measurable. Thoughts?

ben: Do you mean fully async for enrichment or a hybrid sync/fallback?

mae: Hybrid initially. Default path stays minimal sync, heavier enrichment goes to async queue. Provide a sync 'enrich-lite' fallback with bounded latency for critical flows.

olga: Main concern is correctness and product contract. Eventual consistency is ok for some features but not for auth/permissions. Need per-endpoint opt-in.

samir: Staged approach suggestion: 1) Define 'hotpath-core' interface and strip optional enrichment fields, 2) implement sidecar that fans out to async queue + sync-lite, 3) route a % of traffic to the new path via canary header, 4) monitor errors/latency and iterate.

mae: Exactly. Proposed guardrails: - strict protobuf contract for hotpath (only required fields) - timeboxed sync path (e.g., 30–50ms) - backpressure signals in header (X-Hotpath-Budget) - per-tenant rollout flags and quotas.

mae: Example config snippet for the interface and a fallback:
```
rpc Enrich(EnrichRequest) returns (EnrichResponse) {
  // sync budget enforced at edge, fallback to EnrichLite when budget exceeded
  option (sync_timeout_ms) = 40;
}

routes:
  - path: /v1/enrich
    timeout_ms: 30
    fallback: /v1/enrich-lite
```

harper: We should avoid duplicating large models. For enrich-lite we can use a quantized, distilled model on CPU or a cached heuristic layer. Keeps cost low while protecting tail.

ben: Rollout mechanics: add X-Canary:hotpath-core header, start at 1% -> 5% -> 25%. Also need automatic rollback criteria: 99th p99_latency + error_rate + model-quality drift hooks.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary 'hotpath-core' deployed to staging at 1766000300.

olga: Add contract tests and a lightweight semantic diff eval (prompt-based smoke) to catch quality regressions before wider rollout. Tie regressions to Redwood Console alerts.

mae: I'll draft the cutover checklist: 1) spec proto + compatibility rules, 2) sidecar + sync-lite impl, 3) per-tenant feature flag, 4) canary and metrics dashboard, 5) gradual sweep and cleanup of old enrich endpoints.

samir: I'll own the spike for the sidecar and a small PoC of enrich-lite (2 weeks ETA).

ben: I'll run a cost delta for duplication and get back by end of week.

mae: Awesome. If no objections, I'll open an RFC follow-up doc with the checklist and spike owners. Thanks all :rocket:
